lines.japanese: でも、ちょっと困っちってた。
lines.english: But I had a little problem.

lines.japanese: 「うーん……」
おれ、どうしたら帰れるんだろう。
lines.english: How was I supposed to get back?

lines.japanese: 「はやく帰りたいなあ」
lines.english: “I wanna go back soon.”

lines.japanese: もうこんな所とっとと逃げて、楽しいことばっかしてあそびたいなあ。
lines.english: I wanted to hurry up and run away from this place, then play and do nothing but fun stuff again.

lines.japanese: 「ううーん……」
lines.english: “Hmmm...”

lines.japanese: ひっしこいてなやんでると、どんどんアタマが重たくなる。
lines.english: The harder I tried to think, the heavier my head got.

lines.japanese: あーあ……おれ、どうしたらいいかなあ……。
lines.english: Aw, man... What was I supposed to do...?

lines.japanese: おフロん中でたいく座りして、ひとりでずっとかんがえてた。
lines.english: I sat in the bath with my knees hugged to my chest and thought about it all by myself.

lines.japanese: 小ばとはあちこち白いの付いてる体をあらったら「お兄ちゃんはゆっくりあったまってね」てゆって、ひとりで先に出てった。
lines.english: Once Kobato had washed the white stuff off herself, she said, “Take your time and warm up, Big Brother,” and left before me.

lines.japanese: いつのまにかおれら、おフロいっしょに入んのも大へんなぐれー体がでっかくなってたみたいだ。
lines.english: Somehow our bodies had gotten so big that even taking a bath together was a whole huge ordeal now.

lines.japanese: やべーなあ、はやく帰って子どもにもどんなきゃなあ。
lines.english: This was bad. I had to hurry back and turn into a kid again.

lines.japanese: 「はふー」
lines.english: “Haaah.”

lines.japanese: お湯がちょっとあつくて、なんかボーッとしてきたかもしんない。ちょっとアタマがフラフラすっから、ひざの上にアゴのっけといた。
lines.english: The water was a little hot, and maybe it was making me all fuzzy. My head felt dizzy, so I rested my chin on my knees.

lines.japanese: 大人の体は、足とか長すぎておフロん中じゃ超ジャマくさかった。そんでも汗かいてヒーヒーゆいながら、すっげえなやんだ。
lines.english: An adult body had legs way too long for the tub. They got in the way like crazy. Still, sweating and panting, I thought as hard as I could.

lines.japanese: どうすればいいんだろ。やっぱおれ、表に出てこなきゃよかったんだ。ずっと裏のヒミツき地にすっこんでればよかったんだ。
lines.english: What was I supposed to do? I should never have come out to the front. I should've stayed hidden forever in the secret base behind everything.

lines.japanese: だけど気が付いた。おれが帰ったあとのこと。おれがまた裏の暗いトコにすっこんだら、表にのこった小ばとはどうなっちゃうんだろう。
lines.english: But then I noticed something. What about after I went back? If I crawled into the dark place behind everything again, what would happen to Kobato, left out here in front?

lines.japanese: このへんには夢テレビとかないから、ヤなこととかムカつくことがあってもただガマンするしかないのに、おれがいなくても小ばとはひとりでガマンできるのかな。
lines.english: There was no dream TV out here. If something bad happened, or something made her mad, she just had to put up with it. Could Kobato put up with everything all alone if I wasn't here?

lines.japanese: 「はぁ、はぁ……はひぃ……」
lines.english: “Hah... hah... haaah...”

lines.japanese: ああ、どうしよう……困れば困るほどあたまがズンズンおもたくなって、それとやっぱ、お湯がちょっとすげーあつい気ぃして、なんかどんどんボーッとしてクラ～ってしてきた。
lines.english: Oh, what was I gonna do...? The more trouble I was in, the heavier my head pounded. And the water really did feel awful hot now. Everything was getting fuzzier and spinnier.

lines.japanese: 「おれが帰ったら……ポッポさびしがるかな……」
lines.english: “If I go back... will Poppo be lonely...?”

lines.japanese: せっかくおれのかわりにホークを作ってやったのに、聖なるナイトを作ってやったのに、なんでポッポはあいつが兄ちゃんじゃダメなんだろう。
lines.english: I’d gone to all that trouble to make Hawk take my place. I’d made him a holy knight. Why wasn’t he good enough to be Poppo’s big brother?

lines.japanese: ホークはおれなんかより、ずっといいやつだ。おれはむかしっから、ああゆう人げんになりたいって思ってたんだ。だれにでもやさしくて、だれからもきらわれない人げん。超かっけくて超むてき。
lines.english: Hawk was a way better person than me. He was the kind of person I'd always wanted to be: nice to everybody, hated by nobody. Super cool and totally invincible.

lines.japanese: だから、あいつがいるんだから、そんでおまけにイーグルとかファルコンもいるんだから、べつにおれなんか一人ぐらいいなくてもダイジョブなんじゃないかな。
lines.english: So if she had him—and Eagle and Falcon besides—wouldn't everybody be fine if there was one less me?

lines.japanese: いろいろ考えてたら、どんどんボーッとしてきて、いつの間にか目ぇつぶっちってた。
lines.english: The more I thought about everything, the fuzzier I got, and before I knew it I'd closed my eyes.

lines.japanese: そんでなんか、どっかからグイ～って引っぱられてるみたいな感じしてきた。でもおれボーッとしすぎてて、もうそんなんどーでもよかった。
lines.english: Then it started feeling like something somewhere was pulling me in. But I was too dazed to care anymore.

lines.japanese: 「うん……じゃあ……かえろっかな……」
lines.english: “Yeah... Maybe... I'll go back...”

lines.japanese: だって、がんばって表にいたって、もうここにおれの友だちはいない。田ばたも河嶋もタッチンもけんたろーも、一小のみんなはいないんだ。
lines.english: Even if I tried my hardest to stay outside, none of my friends were here anymore. Tabata, Kawashima, Tacchin, Kentaro—everybody from First Elementary was gone.

lines.japanese: ４かいのケン兄もいない。やさしいユキ姉もいない。集めてたカードもない。裏店もないから学こうのかえりにガチャガチャもできないし、もんじゃも食べらんない。家もちがうから、お母さんだって──
lines.english: Ken from the fourth floor was gone. Kind Yuki was gone. My card collection was gone. The little back-alley shop was gone, so I couldn't stop for capsule toys or savory griddle cakes after school. Even the house was different, so Mom—
—Hm?

lines.japanese: あれ、そうだ、そういえばお母さ
lines.english: Wait. Right. Come to think of it, Mo—
“Wah!?”

lines.japanese: 超びびった。おふろのそこが、いきなしガクッてぬけた。
lines.english: It scared me to death. The bottom of the bath suddenly dropped away.

lines.japanese: おれビックリして、あわてて目ぇあけたら──
lines.english: I panicked and snapped my eyes open—

lines.japanese: ──あれ、あけてもまっくらだ。なんだこりゃ。
lines.english: —but even with them open, everything was black. What was this?

lines.japanese: まっくらでなんも見えないけど、んー、なつかしいかんじ。
lines.english: I couldn't see a thing in the darkness. Still, it felt familiar.

lines.japanese: このかんじ……ああ、そっか……。
lines.english: This feeling... Oh. Right...

lines.japanese: おれ帰ってきたんだ……帰りてーって思ったから、帰ってこれたんだ……。
lines.english: I'd come back. I wanted to come back, and that was all it took...

lines.japanese: 「そっかあ」
lines.english: “I see.”

lines.japanese: でも、よかったのかな、これで……。
lines.english: But was this really okay...?

lines.japanese: あたまをうしろにグーっとたおして上のほう見た。ずっと、ずっと、ずーっと先で、おれんコト落っことしたせかいが夜の池にうつったお月さまみたくショボショボゆれてた。
lines.english: I tipped my head waaaay back and looked up. Far, far, faaar away, the world that had dropped me down here wobbled all dim and sad, like the moon in a pond at night.

lines.japanese: 「ひょえー、とおいなあ」
lines.english: “Whoa. That's far.”

lines.japanese: あの向こうにこんどはいつ戻れんのかな。
lines.english: When would I get to go back up there next?

lines.japanese: いつか戻れんのかな。
lines.english: Would I ever get to go back someday?

lines.japanese: ねえ、またいつか戻れんのかなぁ？
lines.english: Hey. Would I ever get to go back?

lines.japanese: ちぇっ、分かんないか。
lines.english: Tch. Guess you don't know either.

lines.japanese: 「ポッポぉ……ごめんなー……」
lines.english: “Poppo... I'm sorry...”

lines.japanese: もし次に小ばとと会えたとき、こんどはあいつ、何才ぐらいになってんのかな。
lines.english: If I ever saw Kobato again, how old would she be by then?

lines.japanese: おばちゃんになってんのかな。おばあちゃんになってんのかな。それとももう死んじゃってんのかな。
lines.english: Would she be middle-aged? An old lady? Or would she already be dead?

lines.japanese: 「えっ？　それはヤだな……」
lines.english: “What? No. I don't want that...”

lines.japanese: あ、そうだ！　おれ小ばとに、なんもゆわないで来ちった。
lines.english: Oh, right! I'd left without saying anything to Kobato.

lines.japanese: やばい、あいつ心ぱいしちゃうよ。そうだ、おれ、もどんないと。おれがおフロから出てくんの、テレビのへやで待ってるってゆってたも。
lines.english: This was bad. She'd worry about me. I had to go back. She said she'd wait in the TV room for me to come out of the bath.

lines.japanese: 「よっ！」
lines.english: “Hup!”

lines.japanese: ショボショボした光につかまろうと思って、手ぇのばしてジャンプした。
lines.english: I jumped, reaching for the faint, trembling light above.

lines.japanese: でもとどかない。全ぜんとどかない。
lines.english: But I could not reach it. Not even close.

lines.japanese: 「よっ！　ほっ！」
lines.english: “Hup! Hah!”

lines.japanese: はやくもどらなきゃ。
lines.english: I had to hurry back.

lines.japanese: こんなとこで夢テレビ見てるばあいじゃないよ。
lines.english: This was no time to sit around watching dream TV.

lines.japanese: 「ンっ！　やっ！　えしょっ！」
lines.english: “Ngh! Hah! Heave!”

lines.japanese: もどらなきゃ。小ばとのとこに行かなきゃ。
lines.english: I had to go back. I had to get to Kobato.

lines.japanese: 大人になんのはヤダけど、小ばとに会えないのはもっとヤダよ。
lines.english: I hated becoming a grown-up, but I hated never seeing Kobato again even more.

lines.japanese: 「ちくしょう！　ちくしょう！」
lines.english: “Damn it! Damn it!”

lines.japanese: なんでおれ、もどってきちったんだ。
lines.english: Why had I come back here?

lines.japanese: あいつはホークとかイーグルとかファルコンじゃなくて、ずっとおれんコトまってたのに。
lines.english: She hadn't been waiting for Hawk or Eagle or Falcon. She'd been waiting for me all this time.

lines.japanese: そんなのに、またおれ逃げてきちった。また小ばとんコトほっぽってきちった。
lines.english: And still I'd run away again. I'd left Kobato behind again.

lines.japanese: 「ふっ、ざけーっ！　ちっ、しょおー！」
lines.english: “Screw... thaaat! D-daaamn it!”

lines.japanese: あったま来て、石とかけっとばしたかったけど、なんも落ちてなかった。ここには、なんもない。石ころも空きカンもエレベーターも、なんもない。
lines.english: I was so mad I wanted to kick a rock, but there wasn't anything lying around. There was nothing here. No stones, no empty cans, no elevators—nothing.

lines.japanese: そしたらどんどんヤぁな気もちになってきちって、なんかすんげー悔しいくて悲しいくてポロポロ泣きたくなってきちった。
lines.english: Then I started feeling worse and worse. I got so mad and sad I wanted to cry and cry.

lines.japanese: 「ぐすっ、すんっ……」
lines.english: “Sniff... sniff...”

lines.japanese: ううう……ちくしょう、もうやだ。
lines.english: Ugh... Damn it. I hated this.

lines.japanese: おれはなんとか泣くのガマンして、とりあいず夢ラジオでも聞いてヤなこと全ぶ忘れようと思った。
lines.english: I somehow kept myself from crying and figured I'd listen to dream radio for now and forget all the bad stuff.

lines.japanese: 「♪たらった～、たったららっ、たったら～、たったらら、たったら～」
lines.english: “♪ Ta-rattaaa, tat-tarara, tat-taraaa, tat-tarara, tat-taraaa...”

lines.japanese: 「翼の折れた天使がセピア色の畦道を駆けだした夜、稚けない臆病者は水田に揺れる銀盤を見た。夜明けの晩に丹頂と象亀が世界の端を滑りおちれば、これが本当の後悔先に立たず。ドァギンコン・キェルーメッシ」
lines.english: “The night the Angel with Broken Wings ran down a sepia country lane, a little coward beheld a silver disk trembling in the rice fields. When, on the night of dawn, the red-crowned crane and giant tortoise slipped over the edge of the world, hindsight came too late. Doagincon Kyerumessi.”

lines.japanese: 「ハ～イお待ちかね、ＤＪコンドルがお送りする『ラブレター・フロムアビス』、えー今夜も禁忌語句ぶっちぎりでね、えー姿なき偉大な勢力に対してこの、いわゆるひとりぼっちのレジスタンス的なスタンスでね──」
lines.english: “Hiii, thanks for waiting! This is DJ Condor with *Love Letter from the Abyss*. Tonight we're blowing straight through the prohibited-phrase barrier again and taking what you might call a one-man-resistance stance against the great invisible powers that be—”
“—Ghk!”

lines.japanese: 「ぐ、く……ぶふっ」
lines.english: “Ngh... bff...”

lines.japanese: 「やっべ……ちょ、痛ててて、ハハ……あのね、これ聞いてくれてるおまえらリスナーたちへ、あの、ラジオ的に説明しちゃうとね、あくっ、あ、あの、いまちょっと、コンドル軽く狙撃されちゃったわけだけれどもね」
lines.english: Oh, man... Ow ow ow. Haha... So, um, for all you listeners, let Condor explain in radio terms: I've just been, y'know, lightly sniped.

lines.japanese: 「あ、あのね、こ、こうゆうね、見えざる理不尽な圧力ってゆうのは、う、あの、いつでもどこでもおまえら出る杭キッズたちを狙ってるわけだけれどね、でも、ね、負けてほしくないってコンドル思うわけなのね」
lines.english: “See, this kind of invisible, unfair pressure is always out there taking aim at kids who stick their necks out. But Condor doesn’t want you to give in.”

lines.japanese: 「そ、そんなわけでね、ハイこれ『ラブレターフロムアビス』奇しくも最終回になってしまったわけだけれども、ぶふ、ＤＪコンドルが今わの際で読んじゃう最後のおたよりは、さ、埼玉県奈落市のＲＮ一番目クンね」
lines.english: Th-that's how it is, folks. Yep, by some strange coincidence, this is now the final episode of *Love Letter from the Abyss*. And the last letter DJ Condor will read on his deathbed comes from radio name Number One, in Abyss City, Saitama.

lines.japanese: 「えー『ＤＪコンドルさん、構成のコンドル林三郎さんこのたびはご愁傷さまです』。あ、ハ～イどうも悼みいりますー。えー『僕は夢ラジオが大好きなので、コンドルさんがいなくなったらとてもとても寂しいです』」
lines.english: Let's see: ‘DJ Condor, and Condor Hayashisaburo, the show's writer: my condolences.’ Ah, hiiii, thank you kindly for mourning me. ‘I love dream radio, so if you disappear, I'll be very, very lonely.’

lines.japanese: 「オーケイありがとう一番目クン。しかし悲しむことはないマイフレンッ！　何故ならばァ、ボクの終わりはキミの始まり。さよなら幻覚、また来て地獄。二度とは会わぬ、方がいい。キンナケン・カル──」
lines.english: “Okay, thank you, Number One! But grieve not, my friend! My ending is your beginning. Farewell, hallucination; welcome, damnation. Better if we never meet again. Kinnaken Kar—”

lines.japanese: <10>\「──バがががががががッ」
lines.english: “—BRATATATATAT!”

lines.japanese: 「番組の途中ですが、ニュース速報をお伝えします」
lines.english: “We interrupt this program with breaking news.”

lines.japanese: 「埼玉県警は先ほど、快感語取締法違反の罪で全獄指名手配中だった男を、こっぴどく射殺したと発表しました」
lines.english: “Saitama Prefectural Police have announced that a man wanted throughout all of hell for violating the Pleasure Word Control Act has been thoroughly shot to death.”

lines.japanese: 「奈落署の調べによりますと、この男は、羽田鷹志の妄想の中で再三にわたりそれらしい言葉を並べたて、長期に渡ってなんやかんやしていた疑いが持たれています」
lines.english: “According to Abyss Precinct, the man was suspected of repeatedly stringing plausible-sounding words together inside Takashi Haneda's delusions and carrying on with this and that over an extended period.”

lines.japanese: 「取り調べに対し男の遺体は『むしゃくしゃしてやった。まさか死ぬとは思わなかった。これぞまさにコンドルは飛んでゆく。なんちゃって』などと供述したのち、親族に見守られながら荼毘に付されてゆきました──」
lines.english: “Under questioning, the man's corpse stated, ‘I was frustrated and just did it. I never thought anyone would die. Talk about “The Condor Flies Away.” Just kidding.’ He was subsequently cremated in the presence of his relatives—”
“Silence, fool!”

lines.japanese: 「ええっ？」
lines.english: “What!?”

lines.japanese: せっかくヤなこと忘れかけてたのに、なんかいつの間ぁにかガルーダがいて、おれの夢ラジオいきなしブン投げてぶっこわしちった。
lines.english: Just when I'd almost forgotten all the bad stuff, Garuda appeared outta nowhere, hurled my dream radio away, and smashed it.

lines.japanese: 「あー、もー、なにすんのよー。もちょっとでヤなこと全ぶ忘れらいたのにー」
lines.english: “Aw, come on! What'd you do that for? I was almost done forgetting everything bad.”

lines.japanese: でもガルーダはおれの文句なんか全ぜん聞いてないくて、じぶんの体（ほんとは体ないけどね）ガリガリかきながらイミわかんないことウバウバどなってた。
lines.english: But Garuda wasn't listening to my complaints at all. He scratched and clawed at his body—even though he doesn't really have one—and yelled a bunch of stuff I couldn't understand.

lines.japanese: 「ああ、暗い暗い暗い、寒い寒い寒い！　ここは萎れる……光を、光をくれ、光をくれェェェ」
lines.english: “Ah, dark, dark, dark! Cold, cold, cold! This place withers me... Light! Give me light! Give me liiiiight!”

lines.japanese: 「はー、どしたん、だいじょぶかー」
lines.english: “Uh, what happened? You okay?”

lines.japanese: 「ややっ！　これは先代、なぜ戻っておられる。よもや貴公……私の厚意を無にしたわけではあるまいな」
lines.english: “What! Former king, why have you returned? Surely you have not thrown my kindness away.”

lines.japanese: 「ねー、かるらー。そんなことよりおれ、また向こうに行きたいんだけど」
lines.english: “Hey, Karura. More important, I wanna go back over there again.”

lines.japanese: 「ほう、奇遇ですな。折りよく私もそう願っていたところです。では父上、共に参りましょう。いや無理だろ。当然でしょう。阿呆か貴様。お忘れか、光の世界へ揚がるには風が、とびきりの強い風が必要で──」
lines.english: “What a coincidence. I find myself wishing the same thing. Then let us go together, Father. No, impossible. Naturally. Are you an idiot? Have you forgotten that to rise into the world of light requires a wind—an exceptionally powerful wind—”

lines.japanese: 「あっ！　かるら、なにあの光！　おわー、キンキラキンだー！」
lines.english: “Oh! Karura, what's that light? Whoa, it's all glittery!”

lines.japanese: 「ふぬん？　ああ、あれはグロリアス・マテリアル、召喚師の用いる触媒です。愚かな貴公が玉座を下りてしまったゆえ、浅ましき者が取って代わろうとしているのでしょう」
lines.english: “Hrm? Ah. That is Glorious Material, a catalyst employed by summoners. Since you, in your folly, abandoned the throne, some wretch must be attempting to take your place.”

lines.japanese: 「えー、だれぇ？」
lines.english: “Who?”

lines.japanese: 「あの音色は聖騎士の呼子……となると泣き虫ホークですな」
lines.english: “That melody is a holy knight's call. It must be crybaby Hawk.”

lines.japanese: 「はー、そーなん。ね、そんで、おれがまた戻るにはどうすればいいの？」
lines.english: “Oh. Okay. So how do I get back again?”

lines.japanese: 「貴公の無知にも困ったものだ……うぉふん、よろしいか父上、ひとつ申しあげておきましょう。承知の通り、現在のグレタガルドは、ホーク・イーグル・ファルコンの三愚弟によって共同統治されております」
lines.english: “Your ignorance is quite a burden... Ahem. Listen well, Father. As you know, Gretagard is presently ruled jointly by the three foolish brothers Hawk, Eagle, and Falcon.”

lines.japanese: 「片や、我らは光射す大地から墜ちたもの。奈落の底に留まるを天命と定められたもの。遺憾ながら、彼らのようにたやすく玉座へ腰を下ろすことは出来ないのです」
lines.english: “We, by contrast, are those who fell from the land bathed in light, those whom fate ordained to remain at the bottom of the abyss. Regrettably, we cannot seat ourselves upon the throne as readily as they.”

lines.japanese: 「でもおれ、いまちょっと向こう行ってきたよ」
lines.english: “But I just went over there.”

lines.japanese: 「しかり。たやすくはないが、不可能ではなかった──」
lines.english: “Indeed. Difficult, but not impossible—”

lines.japanese: 「──ならば、ふたたび光射す園を見下ろす機がいずれ訪れるやもしれません。そのとき来たるまで、父上におかれては奈落の魔性に屈せず抗いつづけておることです」
lines.english: “—which means another chance to look down upon that sunlit garden may someday come. Until that hour, Father, you must resist the demons of the abyss and refuse to yield.”

lines.japanese: 「讒言申しあげますが、耳に障るその奈落弁も控えられた方がよい。これまでのように自ら進んで奈落の魔性を受けいれていては、よしんば幸運の機来たりとも、その風に乗ること適いますまいて」
lines.english: “Allow me one small slander: you would do well to curb that grating Abyss dialect. If you keep welcoming the demons of the abyss as eagerly as you have, then even should fortune send another wind, you will never ride it.”

lines.japanese: 「ならくのましょう？　なにそれ？」
lines.english: “Demons of the abyss? What's that?”

lines.japanese: 「愚問を。むろんあの馬鹿げた退屈凌ぎのことですよ」
lines.english: “What a foolish question. Why, those ridiculous diversions of yours.”

lines.japanese: 「えっ、夢テレビとか夢ラジオのこと？」
lines.english: “What, dream television and dream radio?”

lines.japanese: 「いかにも。あれはいけません。あれは奈落の魔性がもたらす滅びの遊戯です。今後あのような、都合のよい追憶と妄想ばかり縫合した、非生産的なまやかしに耽溺すること一切を禁じさせていただく」
lines.english: “Precisely. They are forbidden. They are games of ruin brought forth by the demons of the abyss. Henceforth, I prohibit all indulgence in such barren illusions, stitched together from convenient memories and fantasies.”

lines.japanese: 「な、なんで？」
lines.english: “Wh-why?”

lines.japanese: 「あの甘やかな幻像は元来、虚無という絶望を生きぬくための逆症療法です。しかしグレタガルドに『王が興じた吟遊詩人の歌も三日続けば騒擾罪』という諺があるように、効きすぎる薬はかえって毒なのです」
lines.english: “Those sweet phantoms began as a remedy by opposites, a means of surviving the despair of emptiness. But as the Gretagard proverb says, ‘When the king's favorite minstrel plays for three days, his song becomes a breach of the peace.’ Medicine too potent becomes poison.”

lines.japanese: 「父上、貴公は地上にいた間、一度ならず奈落の闇を偲び、焦がれ、郷愁を覚えたのではありませんか」
lines.english: “Father, while you were upon the surface, did you not more than once remember the darkness of the abyss, yearn for it, feel homesick for it?”

lines.japanese: 「うん、はやく帰りたいって、何回もおもったよ」
lines.english: “Yeah. I kept thinking I wanted to come back soon.”

lines.japanese: 「ふむん、やはり甘美な惰性に魅了されておいでだ」
lines.english: “Hrm. As I thought: you remain bewitched by its sweet inertia.”

lines.japanese: 「よろしいか、ここは孤独なる深淵、おぞましき闇の底……篤と顧み、篤と胸に刻みなさい。我らは常に彼方の光を仰ぎ、白き空への執着を忘れてはならぬのです」
lines.english: “Listen well. This is a lonely chasm, the bottom of a loathsome darkness. Consider it well and carve it deep into your heart. We must forever gaze up at that distant light and never relinquish our longing for the white sky.”

lines.japanese: 「はー、そーなん。じゃあおれ、がんばる。がんばって、またポッポに会いにいくよ」
lines.english: “Oh. Okay. Then I'll try. I'll try really hard and go see Poppo again.”

lines.japanese: 「うぉんむ、うぉんむ。結構。そのとき私は──かの御子のため──出立する貴公の背に、あえて馬の鼻を向けよう」
lines.english: “Hrrm, hrrm. Excellent. And when you depart—for the sake of that child—I shall turn your horse toward the road ahead and see you off.”

lines.japanese: 「えっ、かるらは行かないの？」
lines.english: “What? You're not coming, Karura?”

lines.japanese: 「愚問を。光の園に玉座はひとつ。すなわち貴公を送りだすということは、おのれをこの闇に縫い……つけ、る……？　ことに？　ほか、ほかっ、ほかならなイッヒイィィィー！？」
lines.english: “What a foolish question. There is but one throne in the garden of light. To send you upward means stitching myself to this darkness... forev... er...? It means... it means—EEEEEEK!?”

lines.japanese: ガルーダがカオまっかにしてフーフーゆいはじめた。がきん、がきん、ってヘンなふうに首とか背中がまがって、目ん玉はギロンチョで、手ぇとか足とかアゴとかブルブルブルブルふるぇーてた。
lines.english: Garuda's face turned bright red, and he started huffing. His neck and back bent with strange clanking cracks, his eyes rolled wildly, and his hands, feet, and jaw trembled and trembled.

lines.japanese: 「お、おおれ、おれっ、俺、とて、まこと申さば、く、くくっ……ぬぎぎ、こ、ここ、このゴブリン脳め、ふ、ふしゅ、ふしゅっ、ふしゅーッ！」
lines.english: I-I... I, even I, to tell the truth, g-grr... ngh, y-you, you goblin-brain, h-hssh, hssh, hsshhh!

lines.japanese: そんでガルーダはグーの手をひらいて、そしたらそこにボワッて黒い火ぃがついた。
lines.english: Garuda opened his clenched fist, and black fire flared in his palm.

lines.japanese: 「認めぬ、俺は認めぬぞ！　さあ剣を抜け、恥さらしの逐電王！　君主が社稷を守らずして何とせん！　一度ならず国の山河・民草に背を向けた貴様に、グレタガルドの栄光が預けられるものか！」
lines.english: “I reject it! I refuse! Draw your sword, shameful runaway king! What use is a sovereign who will not defend the realm? You have turned your back upon Gretagard's mountains, rivers, and people time and again. Its glory cannot be entrusted to you!”

lines.japanese: んー？　よく分かんないけど、あれかなあ、ガルーダも上のせかいに行きたいのかなあ。
lines.english: Hmm? I didn't really get it, but maybe Garuda wanted to go to the upper world too.

lines.japanese: 「かるらー、そいだらさー、おまいもいっしょに行こうよ」
lines.english: Karuraaa, then you come with me too.

lines.japanese: 「がるっ！？」
lines.english: “Garu!?”

lines.japanese: 「えー、行きたくないの」
lines.english: “What, you don't wanna go?”

lines.japanese: 「ざ、戯れ言を。よいか、奈落の名に懸けて、余ほど国をおもんぱかっておる王はおらんのだ！　だが悲しいかな、グレタガルドに玉座はひとつ。そしてプリンセス・ダヴが待ちわびている王は貴様の方なのだ」
lines.english: “D-do not speak nonsense. By the name of the abyss, no king holds his nation dearer than I! Yet alas, Gretagard has but one throne, and it is you whom Princess Dove awaits.”

lines.japanese: 「はー、そーなん。はー、でもイスが一個しかないんだったら、おれら、またひとりになりゃーいいんじゃない？」
lines.english: “Oh. Okay. But if there's only one chair, why don't we all just become one person again?”

lines.japanese: 「ぶほん！　なにをたわけた……世迷いごとだ、できるものか」
lines.english: “Bhof! What idiocy... Mere ravings. Such a thing cannot be done.”

lines.japanese: 「えー、できるでしょー。だって、おれらみんな、さいしょはひとりだったでー」
lines.english: “Sure it can. We were all one person at the start.”
“What...”

lines.japanese: 「だいじょぶだよ、また元にもどるだけだで。おれに任せとけてー。なー。そしたらおまいも、ずっと表に出てられんじゃんかー」
lines.english: It'll be okay. We'll just go back to how it was. Leave it to me, okay? Then you can stay out front forever too.

lines.japanese: 「マジで！？」
lines.english: “Seriously?!”

lines.japanese: 「いいや！　いいや、くだらぬ！　統合だと？　貴様と？　貴様らと？　冗談ではない、虫唾が走るわ！」
lines.english: “No! No, absurd! Integration—with you? With all of you? Do not jest. The very thought disgusts me!”

lines.japanese: 「えー、そおかあ？　どうせ表でんなら、みんないっしょのがいいじゃんなー。ねえ、おまいどう思う？」
lines.english: “Really? If we're going outside anyway, wouldn't it be better if everybody went together? Hey, what do you think?”

lines.japanese: 「くどい！　俺は御免こうむると言ったはずだ！」
lines.english: “Enough! I told you I refuse!”

lines.japanese: 「ちがうてー。かるらじゃなくて、そっちのおまいに聞いてんだでー」
lines.english: Nooo. I wasn't asking Karura. I was asking that other you over there.

lines.japanese: 「はむん？」
lines.english: “Hrm?”

lines.japanese: 「ほう、貴様か……終の子よ、声なき子よ、いつからそこにおった」
lines.english: “Ah. You... Final Child, voiceless child. How long have you been there?”

lines.japanese: 「なんもー。そいつ、さっきからずっといんじゃんか。なー？」
lines.english: “What do you mean? He's been there this whole time. Right?”

lines.japanese: 「るふう……奈落の底で何をしておる、終の子よ、名もなき末弟よ、貴様の役割は王座の監視だろう。そうら、早よう揚がれ。哀れな泣き虫勇者が玉座へ向かっておるぞ」
lines.english: “Rrfoo... What are you doing at the bottom of the abyss, Final Child, nameless youngest brother? Your duty is to watch the throne. Go—rise at once. A pitiful crybaby hero is making his way toward it.”

lines.japanese: 「なあ、かるらー。そいつ誰なん？　おれ、ホークとかイーグルとか、今まで色んなやつ作ってきたけど、こいつだけは作ったおぼえないんだーあ」
lines.english: Hey, Karuraaa. Who's that guy? I made Hawk and Eagle and all kinds of guys before, but he's the only one I don't remember making.

lines.japanese: 「なに？」
lines.english: “What?”

lines.japanese: 「うぉんむ、うぉんむ！　なるほど、道理で不完全な存在なのだな。しかし貴様──終の子よ、名もなき使者よ。なぜ貴様だけが深淵の内と外とを自在に往来できる？」
lines.english: “Hrrm, hrrm! I see. No wonder his existence is incomplete. Yet you—Final Child, nameless messenger—why are you alone able to pass freely within and without the abyss?”

lines.japanese: 「えっ、そうなの？　ひょええ、かっちぇー！」
lines.english: Huh, really? Whoa, that's sooo cool!

lines.japanese: 「買いかぶるな父上。そやつはただの悪趣味な覗き屋だ」
lines.english: “Do not overestimate him, Father. He is merely a tasteless voyeur.”

lines.japanese: 「あーこら、かるらー、あんま新入りいじめんなてー」
lines.english: “Hey, Karura. Don't pick on the new kid.”

lines.japanese: 「ぶはん！　異あらば、いまグレタガルドの白き空に誓ってみせるのだな」
lines.english: “Bah! If you object, then swear it now upon Gretagard's white sky.”

lines.japanese: 「終の子よ、全能にして無力な傍観者よ、貴様はその気まぐれな翼で我らが天地に救いをもたらせ。さあ、誓えるか？」
lines.english: “Final Child, omnipotent and powerless observer: upon those capricious wings, bring salvation to our heaven and earth. Come—can you swear it?”
